questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Robert and Rooney aren’t very good friends although they ________ each other for a long time.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer of this question is **option 2) ' have known'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Using ' have known' in the place of blank space to make the sentence correct.
 
• We should use present perfect tense here . We cannot use past tense '**knew' **as past tense use is not right here . 
 
• We also can not use '**has known'** as it is incorrect because here we are talking about two friends so singular form "has" should not come here.​

**​The Correct sentence is : *** Robert and Rooney aren't very good friends although they*** have known ***each other for a long time.*

​

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

The essay is divided into ﬁve paragraphs and every of these has seven sentences.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. 'and every of these'. **

 
• The usage of 'Every' is incorrect here in this part of the sentence. 
 
• The correct word that should be used instead 'Every' is 'Each'. 
 
• The difference between 'every' and 'Each' is that 'every' is used for 'group of people or objects taken as one' whereas 'each' is used for 'individual' or one (person or object) 
 
• Hence, the sentence will be: The essay is divided into ﬁve paragraphs and **each** of these has seven sentences.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.

Nowadays, digital services have made our cash transactions easier and ________.
questions.solution:
In the last part of sentence "**smoother**" as a adjective should come. Because here one adjective '**easier**' is also in the positive degree so after 'and' next adjective should also be in positive degree. While in options two more adjectives gives the sense of positive degree. They are softer and dearer. But they do not give proper meaning and sense to the sentence. That's why the correct adjective "smoother" should be use here.

The correct sentence is " Nowadays, digital services have made our cash transactions easier and smoother."

• Allegation means a positive assertion especially of misconduct/ an assertion unsupported and by implication regarded as unsupportable. For example- Some former colleagues have made serious allegations against him.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word.

ILLUSION
questions.solution:
• Illusion means an idea or belief that is not true. 
 
• Reality means the state of things as they are, rather than as they are imagined to be. 
 
• Fantasy means a pleasant situation that you enjoy thinking about but is unlikely to happen, or the activity of imagining things like this. 
 
• Hallucination means an experience in which you see, hear, feel, or smell something that does not exist, usually because you are ill or have taken a drug.
 
• So the appropriate antonym of Illusion is Reality. We can understand it from their meaning.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I asked two pedestrians the way to the station, __and neither of them couldn’t__ help me.
questions.solution:
• Here in underlined part "**and neither of them couldn't**" is incorrect here.
 
• Because neither as a word itself is negative we do not need another negative word 'couldn't ' here in the sentence.
 
• 'Neither' alone gives negative meaning which is essential for the sentence by saying "but neither of them could help me."
 
• The use of 'and' is also inappropriate as a conjunction 'but' is more appropriate in context with the sentence.
 
• That's why 'and' is replaced by 'but' here.
 
• The correct sentence should be I asked two pedestrians the way to the station, but neither of them could help me.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

Children are not allowed to use the swimming pool ______they are accompanied by an adult.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. 'Unless' **

__
 
• The condition conveys, 'the children will be allowed to swim only when they are accompanied by an adult with them'. 
 
• The correct word to be used here is 'Unless'. 
 
• 'Unless' is used in a sentence to convey that if the first is fulfilled only then the second will execute. 
 
• Hence, the correct sentence will be: Children are not allowed to use the swimming pool **unless__** they are accompanied by an adult.​

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 1
questions.solution:
In sentence " From this height one ______ see the river and the ﬁeld of ripe corn dotted with the ﬂowers." Here we should use **'could'** as a auxiliary verb which shows conditions and possibility in the past and the present tense.

Other words such as **must** shows compulsion which makes it incorrect.

**Need** is used to express necessity/ duty/ to be want which is also not appropriate with the context.

So the correct option is 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 2
questions.solution:
In sentence "that ______ promised a good harvest." After that **'always' **should come.

Because it is an positive adverb and always follows by positive phrase. So after always promised a good harvest is appropriate here.

Other three words rarely, hardly, never are negative words which does not give positive sense to the sentence. So we cannot use them.

So the correct option is 2.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 3
questions.solution:
The correct word is "needed" for the sentence "The only thing the earth ______ was a downpour or at least a shower."

Because we need adjective to qualify what the earth want.

So** 'needed'** as an adjective is correct.

We cannot use **long** because it shows the period of time.

**Prayed** is past form of pray which means request, or plea.

**Displayed**- to arrange something or a collection of things so that it can be seen by the public which is also not in accordance with context.

The correct option is 3.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 4
questions.solution:
In the sentence "Throughout the morning Paul - who ______ his ﬁelds intimately" the correct word is** knew**. Which is appropriate here to show he knew his field intimately.

**Known** is adjective while we need verb here for the subject.

**Knowing** is also a adjective so it should not use.

**Know** is the verb in present tense is not appropriate with the context.

So the correct option is 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 5

Because first half of the sentence is in the past tense so for rest part we cannot use present tense, present future tense in place of these past perfect should come here.
